article.title: What each message status means
article.excerpt: Four states, and one of them does not belong in the same bucket as the others. Reading suppressed as a failure sends you looking in the wrong place.

head: Status
Meaning
rows: Accepted and handed to the provider. This is where a successful send call lands — not the end of the story
The provider confirmed delivery to the handset
Attempted and refused — either at submission, or later by provider receipt. errorCode carries the reason
Never attempted. The platform stopped it before sending because the recipient had opted out

p: A suppressed message never reached a provider, so there is no provider history to investigate. It is also not billed: providerMessageId and encoding are null, segments is 0, and it does not count toward your monthly totals.
Retrying it will not help — the recipient's opt-out state does not change because you retried. Re-enabling marketing to that number requires the recipient to express consent again.

sections.h: A success code is not a delivery
p: The send endpoint accepts asynchronously. A success response means the platform submitted the message — it may already be on its way, or the provider may refuse it a moment later. The state that tells you the truth is delivered, which arrives by callback or by polling.
sections.scope: Status callbacks cover delivered and failed. A suppressed message has no callback, because its final state was decided at acceptance.
